model_output.score_comment_short: Your management responsibilities are clear, but program results and working details are sparse.
model_output.score_comment_long: The current role names the staff you supervise and the students your program serves. Most bullets describe duties without showing how the work was carried out or what happened. Adding details to the summer program and reporting bullets would make the experience easier to assess.
model_output.score_plain: A reviewer can see your youth workforce management background, but may have trouble comparing your accomplishments with those of other program managers.
model_output.first_impression: Your path from tutoring to youth workforce management is easy to follow. The current role names a substantial staff, while the program itself is described mostly through responsibilities.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: "Recruit and onboard employer partners" doesn't explain how you prepare employers to host students, leaving your contribution to those partnerships unclear.
model_output.summary: Managing a summer jobs program and supervising 4 coordinators and 20 seasonal staff gives your current role a clear management-level frame. The staff detail is worth keeping because it shows the people-management responsibilities behind the title. Your work connects students, employers and funders, but the resume doesn't say how the placements are arranged or what participants achieved. That makes it difficult to distinguish the program's reach and results from its stated purpose.
strengths: The progression from Program Coordinator to Program Manager at Harbor Pathways makes your growth within youth workforce work easy to follow.
City and foundation grant reporting shows that your work includes communicating with different kinds of funders.
Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud is named in Skills, giving a reviewer a specific system to associate with your participant data work.
gaps: The employer onboarding bullet doesn't describe what you do to prepare partners, so the nature of your partner management remains broad.
Participant outcomes are tracked, but the resume doesn't name them or state their results, leaving the program's effects unclear.
Program design appears in Skills without a corresponding example in Experience, making it difficult to see what you designed.
